newsitem.title: USA: USDA says U.S. Nov agricultural exports hit record.
newsitem.headline: USDA says U.S. Nov agricultural exports hit record.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department Tuesday said U.S. agricultural exports were a record $5.9 billion in November and were up 13 percent from the same period a year ago.

In its monthly Agricultural Trade Update, USDA's Economic Research Service said November soybean exports shot up 78 percent from a year ago to 4.1 million tonnes. USDA said much of the increase came from higher shipments to the European Union, which took 1.6 million tonnes in November.

November corn exports were 20 above a year ago at 6.1 million tonnes. Japan was the leading market with 1.4 million tonnes, while corn shipments to South Korea more than doubled from October's total to 1.2 million tonnes, USDA said.
Wheat exports in the month at 2.0 million tonnes were down 29 percent compared with November 1995, USDA said.
It said November cotton exports more than doubled from the prior month to 125,000 tonnes but were off 22 percent compared with November 1995.
